reasoning: Fully integrated into the dialect with ث said as s, so the Arabic is respelt مَسَلَن. The tanwin is genuinely pronounced here, hence -an.
ق in 'abl is a glottal stop, and the hamza after the article prefix is written, il-'akl. walla is the Palestinian or in questions; ba3do carries the -o suffix.
م is a moon letter, so the article stays il-. Long ii in the stressed syllable.
Palestinian says kilme, not kalima, and the construct ending is -et. 7a'' is geminate, so the glottal ق doubles, on the same pattern as 3a''ad.
A written connector; a Ramallah speaker who used it would say been with a long ee, not the MSA diphthong. In conversation it is lamma or wa't ma for simultaneity.
Taa marbuta after ز is e. The word on its own is just a prize; the grand prize is il-jaayze il-kubra.
Long ee, not the MSA diphthong 3ayn. Dual 3eeneen; also means a spring of water.
The Palestinian question word for where, against MSA ayna. Long ee.
English borrowing kept whole in Ramallah speech; the loan v is written v, though many speakers say it as f since Arabic ف is the nearest letter.
ض and ص are emphatic. The dual ending is -een with a long ee. Usually said in full as bi7ajar waa7ad.
b-imperfect plural with ق as a glottal stop. bass at the end is the Palestinian only; the shadda doubles the s.
Form V past with an initial cluster; the shadda doubles the s. Used of health, weather and situations alike.
Plain CaCaC past. Also the everyday verb for withdrawing money, sa7ab maSaari.
Form V with ق as a glottal stop, doubled by the shadda; compare the very common participle mitwa''i3. The MSA reading tawaqqa3 is not what is said in Ramallah.
In Palestinian sharaab means socks, with the plural shraabaat; the MSA sense of a drink or syrup is not the everyday one here.
Two short i vowels in the dialect, nisir; plural nsuur. Strictly a vulture in classical usage, but people use it for an eagle.
The final hamza of shaa' is written, as in maa shaa'. Said when someone brings news that sounds worrying; kheer has a long ee.
b-imperfect second person masculine plus shu, the Palestinian what. Used as a conversational opener.
Form V past; ط is emphatic T and the shadda doubles the w. Often heard as ittTawwa3 with the assimilated prefix.

Romanized as a Ramallah speaker would say it, with ق as a glottal stop; the parenthetical label is not part of the phrase. The Hebron pronunciation the entry points to turns ق into [k] and ك into [ch], which the scheme has no symbols for, and is outside the Ramallah target variety.
ط is emphatic T; ع is a moon letter so the article stays il-. Said to someone who is working; the reply is allah y3aafiik.
Word-initial hamza on a vowel seat, so only the long ii is written. Means the rent payment and, loosely, the renting itself.
The headword spelling بلاندا looks like a slip: the country is بولندا, said boolanda with a long oo. The romanization and vowelling give the name as it is actually pronounced.
Loan via Turkish and French; taa marbuta after م is e. Singular in Arabic even though the English is plural.
Plural shawaarib, which is what people usually say. The identical participle shaarib 'drinking' is a separate word.
